instruction: Using the 2015–2019 American Community Survey 5-year estimates, identify New Mexico counties that simultaneously exhibit large renter populations, notable language barriers, limited internet access, transportation disadvantages, low income, and rental stress. Rental stress higher than the statewide level must be demonstrated by at least one of the following: a share of renter households with a rent-to-income ratio of 35% or higher that exceeds the statewide share, or a share of renter households with more than one occupant per room that exceeds the statewide share. All comparisons of “higher than statewide” or “lower than statewide” use the New Mexico statewide value from the same data release. Separate multiple counties with commas. Percentage fields retain three decimal places with no percent sign. LEPHH and LEPSharePct refer to limited-English-speaking households of any tenure and their share of all households, respectively; the renter-household condition is separate. SevereRentBurdenPct denotes the share with gross rent of 35% or more of household income, excluding households for which the ratio is Not computed.
